_readme: Static background-prompt bank (Phase 16, Plan 16-03) — the 3rd of 3 coexisting background_prompt sources for the Hybrid engine (FAL Flux 2 Pro background + Creatomate typographic overlay). Precedence order everywhere it's consulted: (1) an optional background_prompt field on the incoming brief (user-provided, wins) > (2) GPT-4o's hardened design.background_prompt (openai-text/openai-carousel, see n8n/workflow.json) > (3) this bank, used as the final fallback. Entries seeded from real production briefs in scripts/eval-briefs.json (human-validated in Phase 15) plus new curated variants. The single/story entries for each type are kept byte-identical (first array element) to the inline BACKGROUND_BANK fallback embedded in n8n/workflow.json's parse-content node — if you edit one, edit both.
_rules: NEVER ask for readable text, words, letters, numbers, logos, captions, signs, or any legible UI text of any kind — Flux draws NO text, Creatomate composes ALL text on top.

If a phone/laptop/screen appears in the scene, its screen must show only an abstract glow or blurred shapes — never legible content, not even in English (castellano/legibility hard rule: any chat or phone screen a user actually needs to READ must be composed by Creatomate as real text elements, never left to Flux).

Atmosphere follows brand + slide position: case_study -> warm/emotional human scenes; educational/authority -> tech/modern scenes; carousel slide 1 (opening) -> warm/emotional; carousel middle slides -> tech/modern; carousel closing slide has NO entry here by design (text-only render, no Flux call).
Style always targets the canonical palette: dark background #070A18, purple-to-magenta gradient accents (#8000A8 to #BA00E0), cyan accent #00E5FF. Never the legacy palette.
Every prompt is in English, photorealistic, and fully self-contained (no 'same as above' / 'idem' references).
